  "summary": "Skip advancing generation counters and rotating when re-inserting an element already present in the current generation of a CRollingBloomFilter. Computed hash values are cached in a stack array during the membership check so insertion does not recompute them.",
  "problem": "Inserting the same item repeatedly increments the generation entry counter without adding new membership data. This causes the rolling filter to rotate generations prematurely, expiring older, unrelated entries earlier than its configured capacity guarantees.",

result.summary: Skip advancing generation counters and rotating when re-inserting an element already present in the current generation of a CRollingBloomFilter. Computed hash values are cached in a stack array during the membership check so insertion does not recompute them.
result.problem: Inserting the same item repeatedly increments the generation entry counter without adding new membership data. This causes the rolling filter to rotate generations prematurely, expiring older, unrelated entries earlier than its configured capacity guarantees.
evidence: PR description: "Re-inserting a value already represented by the current generation advances its entry counter without adding membership information. Repeating one value can therefore expire unrelated entries sooner than the configured capacity implies."
result.card: CRollingBloomFilter is modified to detect whether an inserted element is already represented in the current generation, avoiding redundant entry counter increments and filter rotations. Currently, repeatedly inserting the same value advances generations and purges unrelated entries prematurely. Re-inserting elements from older generations continues to consume capacity and refresh their retention.
